assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental and theoretical demonstration that electrons tunnel over 10-25 Angstrom through protein media at rates set by distance, driving force, reorganization energy and the intervening bonds, using photoinitiated ET in ruthenium-modified cytochrome c, azurin and myoglobin. This is a physical mechanism for biological energy conversion stated in quantitative terms and underlies how respiratory and photosynthetic chains work. Few discoveries in bioinorganic chemistry are as clear and as central to my own field.
assessment.attribution: A compact, clearly attributable configuration: Gray and Winkler led the long-running Caltech program with the ruthenium-protein photochemistry. Marcus (already a laureate) and Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton and others supplied theory and parallel work, which the supplied credit does not include, so priority questions about tunneling-pathway theory versus experiment must be handled in the citation wording.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, extensive use in enzyme and respiratory-chain kinetics, and the 1992 Marcus prize already covers the underlying theory. Recognition is timely if not overdue, but the age of the principal actors should be considered.
uncertainties: How the committee would separate the experimental contribution from Marcus-theory credit already recognized in 1992.
Whether pathway-model theory contributors outside the credited names are needed for a fair citation.
Whether the contribution is perceived as a line of work rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyzes N2 reduction to ammonia under ambient conditions, one of the most consequential reactions in chemistry and biology. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and the FeMo-cofactor, including the central interstitial carbide, plus spectroscopic and kinetic work on the E4 intermediates and electron/ATP coupling, give a chemical picture of a very hard mechanism. Structure combined with kinetics is what I value.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first MoFe and Fe-protein structures), Einsle (high-resolution structure and the central light atom) and Seefeldt (mechanistic kinetics and trapping of intermediates) are my preferred trio. Dean and Ribbe were also decisive in genetics and cofactor biosynthesis, so the three-laureate limit leaves a real credit problem, as does the earlier Lowe-Thorneley kinetic scheme, which is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Structure of the resting enzyme is well established and independently confirmed. The turnover mechanism, how N2 binds and which iron sites are involved, is still debated, though cryo-EM and recent turnover structures are narrowing it. Recognition for the structure and cofactor is mature; for the full mechanism it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the catalytic mechanism is settled enough to support a prize citation.
Allocation among five credited people with overlapping but distinct contributions.
Role of Lowe and Thorneley kinetics, who are not credited, is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the concerted movement of electrons and protons, a central principle in respiration, photosynthesis, water oxidation and many electrocatalytic reactions. Experimental frameworks (bond-dissociation free energies, concerted versus stepwise pathways, model systems for tyrosine-radical chemistry) and theory (vibronically nonadiabatic formulations) have shaped how enzymes such as cytochrome c oxidase and photosystem II are understood. It is close to my own interests, though I note the field is broad.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Nocera built the experimental and conceptual framework for PCET in synthetic and biomimetic systems, and Hammes-Schiffer the quantitative theory. Meyer was an early pioneer, which complicates priority and means a three-person selection leaves out a founder. The Committee would need to decide whether this is one discovery or a line of work.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well established and widely applied, but its relevance to biological systems has been mostly shown through models and calculation, and direct confirmation in complex enzymes is incomplete. Timing is plausible, but the committee may prefer a sharper discovery.
uncertainties: Candidacy rests on a line of work spanning many groups rather than a single attributable discovery.
Priority of Meyer versus the three selected names.
How directly model-system results transfer to protein mechanisms such as cytochrome c oxidase.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase and allows stoichiometry, subunit connectivity, ligand and lipid binding of intact complexes, including membrane protein assemblies, to be determined. It made many mechanisms in complex biological machines visible and complements cryo-EM and kinetics. The method has become a standard tool in structural and mechanistic biochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Chait and Robinson pioneered intact protein complexes by electrospray and extended it to membrane proteins and ribosomes; Heck broadened it to large heterogeneous assemblies. Loo, Gross and others contributed earlier or parallel work. The enabling ionization methods were already recognized in 2002, and the committee will ask how much of the credit is distinct.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and routine in many laboratories for over two decades. Interpretation questions remain regarding how well gas-phase structures reflect solution states, but the method is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for ionization methods and with other mass-spectrometry candidates.
Priority among Chait, Robinson, Heck, Loo and Gross.
Limits on how faithfully gas-phase measurements report solution structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR with isotope labeling, residual dipolar couplings, relaxation methods and TROSY-based approaches opened structure and dynamics determination of proteins up to hundreds of kilodaltons in solution, including invisible excited states. It gave direct access to motion on timescales relevant to catalysis and is a method that made mechanisms visible.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay each made distinct decisive contributions (triple-resonance and dipolar-coupling methods; structure calculation and paramagnetic relaxation enhancement; relaxation dispersion and methyl-TROSY). Wagner and Palmer are also credited, and Wuthrich already received the 2002 prize for NMR structure determination, so the new element has to be argued carefully.
assessment.maturity: Methods are very mature and independently adopted worldwide. Recognition is not premature; the question is whether it is distinct enough from the 2002 NMR prize and from 1991 Ernst.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior NMR-related prizes (Ernst 1991, Wuthrich 2002).
Selecting three of five or six credited people.
Whether the committee will see this as methodology rather than a discrete discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses ultrashort XFEL pulses to collect diffraction before radiation damage, from micro- and nanocrystals at room temperature, and enables time-resolved structural movies of reactions in proteins. Time-resolved structures of photoactive proteins and enzymes directly link structure to kinetics, which I find compelling, with the physics background to appreciate the method.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle diffraction-before-destruction work and the Hamburg group; Fromme, with Spence and others, drove the first protein SFX experiments, and Schlichting contributed time-resolved protein dynamics applications. Hajdu, a key originator of the concept, is deceased, and Spence and Boutet are not on the credited list, so attribution is fragile.
assessment.maturity: The first demonstrations date to about 2009-2011 and the method is now routine at several facilities, but the number of new mechanistic insights is still growing. Somewhat early for a prize compared with the other candidates, but the method is clearly established.
uncertainties: Whether key contributors are missing from the credited names, such as Spence.
Hajdu's death limits a fair configuration.
Mechanistic discoveries obtained so far are fewer than the method's promise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnelled energy landscape and minimal frustration principle resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a physical framework for protein folding, and experimental mapping (phi-value analysis and kinetics of folding transition states) tested it. Statistical physics applied to a central chemical problem, with later influence on structure prediction and on understanding of misfolding.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic carried the main theoretical contribution with Bryngelson, whose name is credited too; Fersht led experimental validation and protein engineering methods. Dill's hydrophobic-collapse view is a competing conceptual strand. A configuration pairing theory and experiment is plausible but will leave out Dill and Bryngelson.
assessment.maturity: Broadly accepted and validated by simulation and experiment, with continuing development. The structure-prediction advances recognized in 2024 reduce some urgency but also confirmed the relevance of the field.
uncertainties: Competing conceptual views and priority among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill.
Overlap with the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction.
Whether the theory is seen as a framework rather than a concrete discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent in 2009 to over 25 percent within about a decade, with solution processing and strong defect tolerance. Important and highly cited, with tremendous impact on photovoltaics research, though not in my own field.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (first perovskite-sensitized cell), Park (solid-state cell with long stability) and Snaith (meso-superstructured and planar devices, understanding of carrier physics) are plausible, with Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok also having major claims. The three-person limit creates a difficult allocation and the committee would need priority evidence from the expert reports.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are independently replicated, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved. Recognition may be timely given impact, though stability limits may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial maturity are not yet demonstrated.
Contentious allocation of credit among six credited people.
I am assessing a field outside my own expertise and would rely on expert reports.
